mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month triggers a demand pullback that reduces corporate earnings expectations and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST m/m change < -10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during episodes meeting the dual GDPC1/HOUST trigger condition.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market that increases wage pressures and input costs, compressing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with UNRATE < 5%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings visibility and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO m/m change < -1% for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods of four consecutive months with INDPRO monthly declines exceeding -1%.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both the federal funds rate and consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 12-month moving averages by more than 1.5 standard deviations signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock that increases real interest rates and erodes equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month moving averages by more than 1.5 standard deviations.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in real retail sales (RSAFS) of more than 3% for two consecutive months, in the absence of a corresponding decline in unemployment, signals a demand-side weakness that is not offset by labor market slack, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS m/m change < -3% for two consecutive months AND UNRATE m/m change >= -0.1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods meeting the RSAFS/UNRATE dual trigger.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) acceleration above 150k for three consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion that raises wage growth expectations and input costs, compressing margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS m/m change > 150000 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods of three consecutive months with PAYEMS monthly growth exceeding 150,000.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average by more than 8% signals a housing market recovery that boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (t-test p > 0.05) during periods when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average by more than 8%.
